No objection invalidating a formally stated numbered theorem was found. The abstract's unqualified operator-norm convergence must refer to S_r=Q M_r Q: a bounded full-parity density gives a counterexample to that assertion for the original T_r. Section 18 also contains stale language about the open sublinear regime. The work merits 5.25 on the supplied high-ceiling Millennium scale, with minor revision; originality and broad impact remain unestablished. strengths: Theorem 1 proves linear-order uniform marginals for both weighting and Perron stationary laws, with exponentially many actual slow transfer modes; Proposition 5 separates this from parity heat-bath slowdown.
Theorem 13 identifies and attains the exact critical norm cap 2^(1/s), while retaining any prescribed density floor below one.
Theorems 21 and 23 combine finite strict-tail endpoint attainment with an independent necessary escaped-moment estimate, proving the universal threshold 1+g(K) on (s-1)/s<K<1.
Theorems 24–27 connect the same critical moment budget with growing exact marginal order; positivity after Fourier erasure and the real-exponent quadratic expansion are explicitly justified.
weaknesses: O1, page 1 abstract: operator-norm convergence is not assigned to S_r; it would be false for T_r. Formal Theorems 25–27 correctly use S_r.
O2, page 31 final introductory paragraph of Section 18: the blanket statement that the intervening sublinear regime is open is stale in light of Theorem 27.
O3: external priority is unestablished; targeted checks cannot exclude earlier equivalent operator formulations.
O4: extensive chronology of intermediate results and review artifacts obscures the final theorem architecture.
O5: no sharp square-root marginal transition, joint stationary-marginal endpoint construction, or local/physical application is proved. These limitations are substantially acknowledged.
potential_errors: O1: Reading the abstract as ||T_r-P_rho||->0 is false. For r_L=1+t chi_[L] with fixed 0<t<1, k_L=L-1 and bounded critical moments, ||S_r-P_rho||=t rho^(L/2)->0, but the 1/full-parity Walsh block of T_r-P_rho has off-diagonal entry t(1+rho^L)/2, so its norm stays at least t/2. This is a headline precision issue, not a counterexample to the explicitly stated S_r theorems.
O2: The page-31 description of the unresolved sublinear regime is broader than the actual remaining open window.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact critical density norm classification with endpoint collapse and any fixed positive floor below one, subject to unestablished priority.
The strict-tail universal boundary 1+g(K), including finite-cap attainment at floor K and necessity for arbitrary collapsing families, subject to unestablished priority.

The joint critical-budget separation: collapse with exact marginals through every L^alpha, alpha<1/2, versus S_r rigidity when k_L^2/(L log(L+1))->infinity; the external homogeneous moment inequality is credited prior work.
